canvas-01.description: The lower half of sheet 1 is a strip of South Broad Street, lettered S. Broad (Crosswicks Av.), at the northwest end of Yardville, drawn at 50 feet to an inch below the key map that fills the upper half of the page. North is towards the upper left. South Broad Street runs across the sheet from left to right, 60 feet wide at the left and 50 feet at the right, where it continues on sheet 2. Kirby Road leaves it to the south a third of the way from the left edge. The strip is a residential frontage: a row of one-, two- and two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings with small outbuildings and garages on long lots on both sides of the street, in blocks 15 and 16 south of the street and block 17 north of it, with a few stores and sheds and a concrete block garage. Kirby Road is a short street with a few garages along it; a note at its lower end gives the distance of 160 feet to the fire department. A large compass rose and the scale of feet are drawn in the open land of block 17 and at the bottom of the sheet. The upper half of the sheet, not covered by this part, holds the key map of Yardville and Groveville at 500 feet to an inch, the title cartouche (June 1927, population 900), the key, notes on water facilities and the fire department, and the street and specials index.
notes: Kirby Road is today Joe Dimaggio Drive; its junction with South Broad Street was detected.
The key map in the upper half of the sheet (500 feet to an inch) is not georeferenced.
Placed from the Kirby Road junction and a building corner carried from sheet 2 (helmert); scale and rotation agree with sheet 2.

Sheet 1: upper half is the key map (500 ft to an inch), title, key and index (not georeferenced); lower half is a 50 ft strip of S. Broad (Crosswicks Av.) with Kirby Rd (today Joe Dimaggio Drive). One part.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: key map of Yardville and Groveville at 500 ft to an inch in the upper half of the sheet (key map, not a to-scale sheet for georeferencing).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows South Broad Street (also lettered Crosswicks Avenue) running straight down the middle of the sheet from the Pennsylvania Railroad to the crossing with Groveville and Hamilton Avenues at the bottom edge, the northern approach to the centre of Yardville. North is towards the upper right. The tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad Amboy Division cross the sheet near the top, with the freight house and passenger station west of South Broad Street and a railroad siding curving away to the lower left past the T. B. Anderson and Son coal yard. The sheet is dominated by industry. West of the street are the Koller Bros. Co. coal yard, the Martin Bros. garage and the Fisk Flap Tube Rubber Co. works (rubber mill, packing room, machine shop, reservoir and a 40,000 gallon tank on a steel tower). East of the street, between the railroad and Grant Avenue, is the large Chandler Palruba Co. linoleum factory, with its machine shop, mixing and grinding rooms, printing house, long dry rooms, reservoir and water tower. Grant Avenue runs east from South Broad Street below the factory, and Hamilton Avenue crosses the lower right corner. The rest of the sheet holds frame dwellings along South Broad Street, among them the post office north of the railroad and a house named Fairview, with open land in blocks 16, 19 and 20. The areas at the left and right edges are marked no exposure. House numbers along South Broad Street run from 101 to 136, and the street is lettered 50 feet wide. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: South Broad Street keeps its name; Hamilton Avenue is today Yardville-Hamilton Square Road and Groveville Avenue is Church Street.

The Pennsylvania Railroad Amboy Division is abandoned east of South Broad Street; the siding to the west survives as the Robbinsville Industrial Track, whose end at South Broad Street was used as a control point.
Grant Avenue could not be matched to a modern street.
Works of note: Chandler Palruba Co. linoleum factory, Fisk Flap Tube Rubber Co., Koller Bros. Co. coal yard, T. B. Anderson and Son coal yard, Martin Bros. garage.
50 ft. S. Broad St from the PRR Amboy Division to Groveville/Hamilton Avs; Chandler Palruba linoleum factory, Fisk Flap Tube Rubber Co. Grant Av not matched to a modern street.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the centre of Yardville, south and east of the crossing where South Broad Street meets Groveville Avenue and Hamilton Avenue at the top right corner of the sheet. North is towards the upper right. From that crossing Crosswicks Avenue (the continuation of South Broad Street) runs down to the lower left and Allentown Road runs straight down the right side of the sheet; Groveville Avenue runs off to the left across the top. Bordentown Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally from the upper left, crosses Crosswicks Avenue at mid-sheet and meets Allentown Road near the bottom right, where it continues eastward as Robbinsville Road. Yardville Run winds down through the large open block 30 from Groveville Avenue, passes under Crosswicks Avenue and Allentown Road and leaves the sheet on the right; Doctors Creek appears in the lower left corner. Most of the sheet is open land in large blocks with scattered frame dwellings. The village buildings cluster near the two ends of Allentown Road: the Yardville Public School and the Jr. O.U.A.M. Hall on Bordentown Avenue, the Presbyterian church and the Yardville National Bank at the top right, a row of dwellings and stores with an auto repair shop along Bordentown Avenue near Allentown Road, and the Yardville Hotel at the corner of Allentown and Robbinsville Roads. Street widths of 38 to 60 feet and house numbers in the 200s and 300s are lettered along the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Groveville Avenue and Hamilton Avenue form today's Church Street and Yardville-Hamilton Square Road; Crosswicks Avenue is today South Broad Street; Allentown Road is Yardville-Allentown Road.
Bordentown Avenue and Robbinsville Road follow the line of today's NJ 156.
The crossing of South Broad Street with Groveville and Hamilton Avenues was hand-picked; the detector did not find it under the title cartouche.
Buildings of note: Yardville Public School, Jr. O.U.A.M. Hall, Presbyterian church, Yardville National Bank, Yardville Hotel.
50 ft. Village centre: Groveville Av (Church St), Hamilton Av (Yardville-Hamilton Square Rd), Crosswicks Av (S Broad St), Allentown Rd, Bordentown Av / Robbinsville Rd (NJ 156).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the southwest side of Yardville along Bordentown Avenue, west of its junction with Groveville Avenue and Court. North is towards the top of the sheet, turned about 30 degrees to the right. Bordentown Avenue, lettered 50 to 60 feet wide, crosses the sheet from left to right just above the middle, with a row of frame dwellings and stores along its north side between the left margin and Railroad Avenue. Railroad Avenue runs from Bordentown Avenue up to the top of the sheet towards the railroad, lined with small dwellings on narrow lots. At the right, Groveville Avenue leaves Bordentown Avenue towards the lower left and crosses Doctors Creek on an iron bridge near the bottom of the sheet; Court runs down the right edge, and a lane (block 44) links the two. A second lane runs south from Bordentown Avenue past Acton Place, a short arbitrary-numbered court. The idle Enterprise Rubber Co. works (dyeing, mixing and packing building, dipping room and office, marked not in operation) stands in the angle between Bordentown and Groveville Avenues, and the Brown and Stouts cement block works is at the top right. The lower left is open land crossed by the Tail Race, with the ruins and foundations of a former mill and a spring house beside Doctors Creek. The left and bottom margins are marked no exposure. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch; house numbers in the 300s.
notes: Bordentown Avenue follows the line of today's NJ 156; Groveville Avenue is today Church Street.
The lower end of Railroad Avenue at Bordentown Avenue was matched to today's Martins Lane; its upper part has no modern counterpart.
Placed from two junctions about 70 m apart (Groveville Avenue and Railroad Avenue on Bordentown Avenue) as a helmert fit; rotation and scale rest on those two points.
Works of note: Enterprise Rubber Co. (not in operation), Brown and Stouts cement blocks, ruins of a mill on the Tail Race.
50 ft. Bordentown Av (NJ 156) west of Groveville Av; Railroad Av (lower end = Martins Lane), Court, Acton Pl, Enterprise Rubber Co.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the eastern side of Yardville, east of Allentown Road, and is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, half the scale of the village sheets around it, with north towards the upper right. Allentown Road runs down the left side of the sheet; Robbinsville Road crosses the top from the upper left towards the lower right. Between them lies a newly laid-out grid of streets: Van Kannel, Clarendon, Springdale and Carlisle Avenues run across the sheet from Allentown Road, and Arlington and Woodside Avenues run parallel to it. The blocks of this subdivision (blocks 33 to 38) are divided into regular narrow lots, and most are still empty; the buildings are scattered frame dwellings with small outbuildings, coops and sheds, and a few auto repair and auto paint shops. Locust Avenue and Highland Avenue run north from Robbinsville Road at the top of the sheet, with a handful of houses along them. West of Allentown Road, in block 46, is Springdale Park, a pleasure ground beside a dammed pond: an auditorium, a kitchen and dining hall, a band stand, a club, an office, a check room, swings and rows of booths are drawn along the water. The southern and eastern parts of the sheet are open land marked no exposure. The top left corner of the sheet repeats the end of Crosswicks Avenue from sheet 3. Most streets are lettered with their widths of 45 to 50 feet, and house numbers in the 400s are given along Allentown Road, Robbinsville Road and the cross streets.
notes: Allentown Road is today Yardville-Allentown Road; Robbinsville Road across the top of the sheet is today NJ 156 (Yardville-Hamilton Square to Robbinsville highway).
The modern Robbinsville Road that crosses Woodside Avenue between Van Kannel and Clarendon Avenues is a later alignment not drawn on the sheet; it was left out of the control.
Highland Avenue could not be matched to a modern street with confidence and was not used for control.
Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; the fitted scale agrees with that.

100 ft. East side: Allentown Rd grid (Van Kannel, Clarendon, Springdale, Carlisle, Arlington, Woodside), Robbinsville Rd (NJ 156), Springdale Park. Modern Robbinsville Road here is a later alignment; Highland Av not matched.

sheet-6-1.description: Sheet 6 shows the village of Groveville, south of Yardville, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right; this part is the sheet less the separate block in its upper right corner. Church Street comes down from the upper right and meets Main Street, which runs across the lower third of the sheet. Church Street is lined on both sides with closely spaced two-storey frame dwellings on narrow lots, with a club house and the post office near Main Street. East of Church Street stand the Groveville Public School, the Groveville M. E. Church with its cemetery, and E. Borden's mince meat factory. Main Street carries a continuous row of frame dwellings and a few stores on both sides, numbered in two series, with a private drive running north from it towards the railroad side of the sheet. The land south of Main Street (block 51) and the lower margin are largely open and marked no exposure. The left edge continues on sheet 7.
notes: Church is today Church Street (the southern continuation of Groveville Avenue); Main is today Main Street.
Placed from the single detected junction of Church Street and Main Street, with the scale set to 8.1 px per foot and rotation from the measured street lines (anchored part, low confidence).
Buildings of note: Groveville Public School, Groveville M. E. Church, E. Borden's mince meat factory, post office, club house.
50 ft. Two parts: 1 Groveville (Church and Main); 2 upper right block beyond a heavy line: Martin Bros cement blocks, Railroad Av and PRR (no junction; unplaced).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: upper right block: Martin Bros cement block works, Railroad Avenue and the PRR Amboy Division (blocks 21 to 23) (no street junction; Railroad Avenue has no modern counterpart beyond its lower end and the railroad is abandoned; needs step 6b: parcel corners or a feature shared with sheet 4).

sheet-7-1.description: The upper part of sheet 7 shows the west end of Groveville around the Morris and Co. Inc. mill, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Crosswicks Creek curves across the top of the part, and a second channel of the creek crosses the left side. Main Street enters at the lower left over an iron bridge across the creek, turns east and runs across the part towards the right edge; Allen Street branches off it to the lower right at the right side of the part. Most of the part is taken by the Morris and Co. Inc. duck and cordemon carpets mill, under mutual risk: spinning and carding, twisting, beaming, weaving and storage buildings, a basket department, machine shop, carpenter and machine shop, engine rooms, picker house, cotton house, cloth storage and a manufactory, with water pipes, hydrants and a note on the watchman, power, heat and sprinkler arrangements. A lumber shed stands by the bridge. Along Main Street east of the mill are an office and a few dwellings, and on Allen Street a brick-lined hall and several two-storey dwellings. Blocks 40, 41 and 49 are numbered on the part; the lower part of the sheet is a separate part below the heavy line.
notes: Main is today Main Street and Allen is Allen Street; the road from the iron bridge is today Groveville Road.

Placed from a hand-picked point at the Main Street / Allen Street fork with the scale set to 8.1 px per foot and north from the direction of Main Street (anchored part, low confidence). The bend of Main Street at the bridge then lies about 20 m from the bend of the modern road.
Works of note: Morris and Co. Inc. duck and cordemon carpet mill.
50 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: 1 Morris & Co. carpet mill, Main and Allen at the Groveville west end; 2 Main, Allen and Asey Lane east of the fork.

sheet-7-2.description: The lower part of sheet 7 continues Groveville eastward along Main Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with Main Street running straight across the middle of the part and north towards the upper right. Crosswicks Creek crosses the upper left corner. Allen Street leaves Main Street at the left edge and runs to the lower right, and Asey Lane links Allen Street with Main Street. North of Main Street (block 41) is a row of two- and two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings and stores, with the Groveville Fire Dept. Co. No. 1 house behind them. South of Main Street (block 51) a long row of identical double dwellings on narrow lots fills the right half of the part, numbered in two series; an orchard lies behind them. A few dwellings stand on Allen Street and Asey Lane in blocks 49 and 50. Main Street is lettered 40 to 45 feet wide and continues on sheet 6 at the right edge.
notes: Main is today Main Street and Allen is Allen Street; Asey Lane has no modern counterpart in OpenStreetMap.

Placed from the tip of the block between Main and Allen Streets carried from sheet 7 part 1, with the scale set to 8.1 px per foot and north from the direction of Main Street (anchored part, low confidence). Main Street continues onto sheet 6 part 1 within about 3 m across the join.
Buildings of note: Groveville Fire Dept. Co. No. 1.
50 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: 1 Morris & Co. carpet mill, Main and Allen at the Groveville west end; 2 Main, Allen and Asey Lane east of the fork.
